title: The Phantom Ballroom
intro: A waltz plays from nowhere. Dancers you cannot see sweep past you in the dust. The orchestra pit hides a vault that has been waiting for the last dance.

objects.label: Dancing Mirror
objects.reward_text: Your reflection does not copy you. It lunges.

a_piano: Start with the clue that rules out the most positions, such as a figure at an end.
Work out which figures are certainly NOT next to each other, then try the possible arrangements.
From the left, the order begins: Cook, Baron.
The full row from the left is: Cook, Baron, Heir, Butler, Doctor, Duke. The answer is the Butler. The vault's character number 1 is T.
b_chandelier: Take the differences between neighbours. Then take the differences of those differences.
First differences: 7, 9, 11, 13, 15. The second differences are all the same: 2.
A constant second difference of 2 means the rule has the form 1n^2 + bn + c. Use the first terms to find b and c.
The rule is 1n^2 + 4n + 3. For n = 12 that is 195. The vault's character number 2 is 7.
c_gramophone: You need exactly (width) steps right and (height) steps up, in some order.
The number of routes is the number of ways to choose which steps are 'right'.
That is C(9, 5), the number of ways to choose 5 items from 9.
The answer is 126. The vault's characters number 3 and 4 are Q and D.
vault: The code has four characters. Some are letters, some are digits.
Each solved object revealed part of the code. Check the vault display.
The pieces go in the order they sit on the vault: Grand Piano, Chandelier, Gramophone.
